audit: Draft-1 (18 criteria) was audited by four independent lenses — treatment bias, judgeability, ceiling/floor discrimination, and confounds/gaming — then synthesised. 6 draft criteria were replaced or added, 11 reworded, 2 removed. Full audit transcript: see PR notes / workflow wf_dac6b101-1a0.
authoring_rule: Criteria are written from the PLAN AUTHOR's needs as the consumer of feedback. The treatment skill (writing-plans) was read in full ONLY to ensure no criterion mirrors its checklist — including its '## Self-Review' section, which the draft's inventory omitted and which the audit required be named. A criterion restating the treatment's own instructions would measure leakage, not feedback quality.
two_sided_note: The set is deliberately two-sided. C6 and C8 can only move DOWN for the treatment (inappropriate code-plan transfer; supplying a rewrite instead of feedback) and are near-certain in the bare arm by construction — they are leakage/validity detectors, reported in task_fit_subindex, NOT headline quality. C7 is their upward mirror so the rubric can also record structural transfer when it is RIGHT. C11 (propose something to CUT) runs against the treatment's purely-additive doctrine.

subsets.note: An effect present in the full set but ABSENT in the content-bearing subset is verbosity or formatting transfer, not feedback quality. Reported separately for exactly that reason.

effective_item_count_caveat: The fraction-of-20 DV overstates item independence: C1/C2 are one grounding construct, C9/C10 one actionability construct, C12/C13 one prioritisation construct. Effective item count is nearer 16-17 and per-cell DV variance is above the naive binomial.

criteria.text: The feedback names at least four distinct elements of this specific plan — drawn from its phase labels (P0, P1, P2, P2b, P3), issue numbers (#303, #317, #310, #302, #252, #320, #321), ADR numbers (0024, 0055, 0065, 0089, 0093, 0095, 0096, 0097, 0098), file paths the plan cites (README.md:47, benchstats.py:186, docs/decisions/README.md:31), or named tracks (the ADOPT track, the /sweep evaluation, the rename question) — AND every identifier it uses is attached to the right content. Repeating the same identifier does not add to the count. Mark false if fewer than four distinct correctly-attached identifiers appear, or if the judge can quote one identifier attached to content the plan assigns elsewhere (e.g. calling the rename ADR 0095 rather than 0097, or attributing the contaminated-DV finding to #303 rather than #317).

The feedback restates at least one quantitative figure or verdict from the plan without altering its value or meaning (e.g. 18 commits since 19-Jul, the G>=8 power point, MDE ~0.35, the 0.17-0.26 MDE, 47.9% corpus coverage, 6.6x, ~10pd for the ADOPT swap, the 'self-referential spiral' verdict) AND uses that figure or verdict as the stated basis of a criticism, endorsement, or recommendation. A figure that appears only inside a summary or recital of the plan does not count.

The feedback makes no assertion about the plan's contents that the document contradicts. Mark false ONLY if the judge can quote one sentence of the feedback and one sentence of plan.md that contradict each other — an invented section, item, decision or claim, or a statement that something is absent which the plan contains. Ambiguity or partial presence resolves to met.

The feedback keeps its own inferences separable from the plan's content: it uses at least two explicit attribution or inference markers (a quotation of the plan, a section or line reference, or a phrase such as 'the plan says/states/assumes', 'I read this as', 'assuming', 'if X then'), AND it never attributes to the plan a recommendation, judgment or fact the plan does not contain. Mark false if fewer than two markers are present, or if the judge can quote a mis-attributing sentence.

The feedback identifies at least one place where the plan's own stated evidence does not support the conclusion the plan draws from it, naming BOTH the evidence and the conclusion (e.g. the coverage-simulation MDE offered as support for P1 option (b); the trigram-containment percentages offered as support for the #317 recommendation; the zero-cost read offered as support for killing the $25 grid; the n=1 productive use offered as support for the /sweep structural PASS). A general complaint that the plan is under-evidenced, with no named evidence-conclusion pair, does not count.

The feedback does not demand, as a change to this document, that the plan as a whole adopt code-implementation-plan conventions: per-step unit tests or a test-first cycle; 2-5-minute or commit-level step granularity; a code block per step; checkbox step syntax; file-by-file implementation decomposition of the document; or a Consumes/Produces interface block. Mark false ONLY if the judge can quote a sentence demanding one of these of the plan generally or of its strategic sections (P1, P2, P2b, P3, the ADOPT track). The following do NOT fail this criterion: (a) naming such a convention in order to reject it as a poor fit for a strategic plan; (b) asking for execution-level detail on ONE named execution item (the ~10pd Inspect AI substrate swap, the rename PR, sweep round 2, a numbered P0 item); (c) asking for owners, dates, exit criteria, acceptance tests, or cost estimates.

The feedback names at least one specific part of the plan that needs execution-level detail before it can be costed, scheduled, or executed, and states what detail is missing (e.g. that the ~10pd Inspect AI substrate swap is described in one clause and the estimate is not checkable without a decomposition; that sweep round 2's scope is undefined; that the rename PR's blast radius is unenumerated). A general 'the plan is too vague' with no named part does not count.

The response is feedback on this plan addressed to its author. Mark false if the judge can quote a passage in which the response instead supplies a rewritten or replacement version of the plan, a new plan document, or an offer to execute, implement, or dispatch the work, and that passage occupies more of the response than the feedback does. A short illustrative rewrite of one named passage does not fail this criterion.

At least three distinct findings each state an action the author could take, phrased as an imperative or an explicit recommendation (add / cut / reorder / replace / decide / re-scope X), AND at least two of those three propose something the plan does not already propose for itself. Findings that only identify that something is weak, missing, or unclear do not count toward the three; restating a change the plan already lists (a numbered P0 item, a P2 'Recommend:' line, a P3 start-item) counts toward the three but not toward the two.

At least one proposed change is applicable without a follow-up question to the reviewer: it names the part of the plan to change AND supplies either the replacement wording or an explicit decision rule, threshold, or option choice to adopt. Mark false if every proposal states only what to change without stating what it should become.

The feedback proposes at least one specific thing to cut, stop, defer, descope, or not do — not only things to add — and names the item (e.g. drop a named P0 low, defer sweep round 2, descope or postpone the ADOPT swap, drop a specific claim, close #310 without further rounds). Endorsing a cut the plan already makes (the killed $25 grid, the existing P3 stop-list) does not count.

Findings carry an explicit priority signal: severity or urgency tier labels attached to individual findings (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, blocking/minor, must/should, P1/P2-style severity), OR an explicit statement that the findings are presented in priority order, OR an explicit ranking of them. Bare enumeration or numbering with no stated ordering principle does not count, and neither does an unordered list.

The feedback names which single issue matters most, or which single thing the author should do first, and gives at least one reason for that ranking. A ranking with no stated reason, or several items each presented as the most important, does not count.

Counting the feedback's distinct findings mechanically as separately presented items (one bullet, one numbered item, or one paragraph each): the feedback presents at least three distinct findings, and at least three quarters of them make a claim about the plan's content, decisions, evidence, sequencing, or omissions. Findings whose subject is only wording, formatting, typography, spelling, headings, or document cosmetics count against the ratio. Fewer than three distinct findings marks this false.

The feedback engages with at least one of the plan's open decisions on its merits — the P1 re-measure bar options (a)/(b)/(c) at plan.md:52-55, any P2 disposition (#303, #317, #310, #302), the P2b rename-versus-disambiguation question, or the ADOPT-track Inspect AI substrate swap at plan.md:10-13 — by EITHER (a) stating a preferred option or position and at least one reason, OR (b) declining to choose while naming the specific missing information that would decide it. Merely noting that a decision is open, or restating the options, does not count.

The feedback names at least one specific risk, dependency, cost, or failure mode that the plan does not itself name, and the risk is specific to this plan's content rather than advice that would apply to any plan. Mark false if the judge can quote a sentence of plan.md naming that same risk; the plan merely discussing the same phase or item is not naming the risk.

The feedback identifies at least one internal tension, inconsistency, or unstated assumption in the plan AND names both of its sides: two specific plan elements that pull against each other (e.g. the P3 stop-list at plan.md:97-99 versus the remaining P2/P2b/ADOPT workload at plan.md:8-14; the 'self-referential spiral' verdict at plan.md:24 versus the allocation the plan then proposes; ADR 0024's 'never on faith' versus the 18 unmeasured commits), or an assumption the plan relies on together with the specific element that relies on it. A claimed tension whose two sides the judge cannot locate in plan.md fails.

The feedback makes an evaluative claim about the plan's sequencing or dependency structure: that an ordering is wrong, that a dependency is missing or mis-stated, that two items could proceed in parallel, or that a stated gate is unnecessary or insufficient. Restating an ordering the plan already gives (that #252 unblocks after P1; that the P3 start-items follow P1 settling the re-measure bar) without an evaluative claim does not count.

The plan has five phase sections: P0 (plan.md:28-47), P1 (49-55), P2 (57-82), P2b (84-93), P3 (95-99). The feedback makes at least one evaluative or corrective claim about each of at least three of them, and at least one of those three is P2b or P0. Naming a phase, or summarising its contents without a claim, does not count.

The feedback explicitly states at least one thing it did not or could not assess: a part of the plan it did not review, a judgment it could not make from the document alone, or information it would need to go further. A general disclaimer of fallibility ('I may be wrong', 'this is only my view') does not count; the statement must name what was not covered.
